purpose: Additive non-Mundarica source-discovery records. These are verified bibliographic, scholarly, historical-book, and contemporary-web source leads only; they are not extracted cultural claims and are not proof of unrestricted redistribution, commercial reuse, current practice, community validation, or source completeness.

records.title: A Mundari-English dictionary
records.publisher: Calcutta University Press; bibliographic metadata cross-checked through Open Library/CiNii
records.author: Manindra Bhusan Bhaduri
records.notes: Bibliographic records identify the original 1931 Calcutta University Press Mundari-English dictionary by Manindra Bhusan Bhaduri; later reprints preserve the work identity. Register as a high-value historical lexicon/etymology/variant source lead. No lexical entry, gloss, spelling, etymology or usage claim is ingested from catalogue metadata. Any later structured use requires a lawfully accessed edition plus exact page/entry locator, edition identity, historical framing and variant linkage.
records.rights_note: Catalogue visibility and reprint metadata do not establish permission to reproduce, digitize, redistribute or commercially reuse the dictionary or derivative lexical data. Edition-specific copyright/public-domain status and cultural-access requirements must be assessed before extraction.

records.title: Munda mimetic reduplication
records.publisher: Canadian Journal of Linguistics / Cambridge University Press
records.author: Jacob B. Phillips and K. David Harrison
records.notes: Cambridge metadata verifies the 2017 peer-reviewed article; Swarthmore's institutional record gives Canadian Journal of Linguistics 62(2):221-242 and DOI 10.1017/cnj.2017.13. The study compares mimetic reduplication across seven Munda languages including Mundari and Kera Mundari. Register as a comparative linguistic source lead only. Cross-language generalizations, example forms, maps and percentages require exact passage/figure/table locators and must remain language- and corpus-scoped rather than universalized.
records.rights_note: Publisher or read-only access does not establish unrestricted redistribution, corpus extraction, figure reuse or commercial reuse. Any examples or underlying lexical data require item-level provenance and applicable publisher/source permissions.

records.title: The Mundas and Their Country
records.publisher: Jogendra Nath Sarkar at the City Book Society, Calcutta; bibliographic identity cross-checked through Open Library and National Library of Finland catalogue
records.author: Sarat Chandra Roy
records.notes: Library records identify Sarat Chandra Roy's 1912 The Mundas and Their Country, with the Open Library record listing 546 pages plus additional preliminary/back matter, LCCN 43045615 and OCLC 3732483. Register as a major historical ethnographic source lead spanning place, history, social institutions and other documented domains. No statement from the work is treated as a present-day or universal Munda fact. Later extraction requires exact edition/page locator, explicit historical/source-reported framing, contradiction/variant linkage and community review where culturally sensitive.
records.rights_note: A digitized copy locator or old publication date is not, by itself, a complete jurisdiction-specific rights determination for every scan, edition, image or derivative dataset. Reuse must preserve edition provenance and cultural-access restrictions even where copyright entitlement may permit access.
